我对记者会的理解是偏hawkish一点点：Warsh说，美联储已经明确展示了“随时采取行动的准备和意愿”——即后续加息仍在桌面上。但他同时说，Fed已经开始看到“金融条件发生变化”。这里大概率就是指向近期长端美债收益率、信用融资成本和AI相关资产波动已经自行收紧。企业投资仍可能以两位数速度增长，因此暂停不是因为经济衰退或需求崩塌。

之后他继续没有直接回答12月会不会加息，仍拒绝传统forward guidance。但是他说，经济和通胀本来支持继续加息，但债券市场与金融条件已经替Fed踩了一部分刹车，因此Fed可以先等数据，而不是今天机械加息。

这相当于给出了一个新的reaction function：

如果股市继续涨、信用利差收窄、长端收益率回落，金融条件重新放松，12月加息概率上升。

如果长端利率继续维持高位、信用市场恶化、AI融资链条继续去杠杆，市场本身的收紧可以替代部分Fed加息。可能后续就不会加息。

fed的意思是，金融风险已经非常大了，所以不能加息，我无法把这个话理解成鸽。

说实话，有一点点恶心。

What should we be watching in the current supercycle?

Japan’s conservative approach to capacity expansion, and the opportunity it creates for Chinese materials, components, and equipment suppliers to move upmarket.

Sinocera (国瓷材料) recently said at an earnings briefing that its key raw materials for high-end MLCCs had passed qualification at some customers.

Sinocera is a China-based materials company that supplies ceramic dielectric powders, a critical raw material for MLCCs. This market was long considered the exclusive domain of Japanese suppliers. Chinese companies, to the extent that they participated, were generally seen as serving only the low end.

But demand is surging, while Japanese companies remain far too cautious. Just look at Murata’s president telling the media that no one knows when the AI supercycle might end. Japanese companies are being excessively conservative.

That is why Japan will inevitably cede market share to China.

And the implications extend well beyond the current cycle. How much capacity will China add in the next cycle? How much more market share will Japan have to give up? Once customers have qualified Chinese suppliers to meet rising demand, they will continue using them during the downcycle as well. That will put even greater pressure on Japanese companies when the cycle turns.

Frankly, I find Taiwanese stocks more attractive than Japanese materials and components plays.

A very sharp friend of mine sent me a take arguing that Cerebras chips could depreciate extremely quickly. I thought I’d share it here.

Cerebras’ wafer-scale engine (WSE) and routing architecture do seem fully capable of solving the yield problem, as the company claims. The uncertainty is around how long the wafer will actually last in operation.

Cerebras’ design requires a large number of redundant interconnects to accommodate manufacturing defects. But all that BEOL wiring significantly increases the effective area susceptible to TDDB (time-dependent dielectric breakdown), potentially creating much greater long-term reliability risks. TDDB can cause shorts, which are more dangerous than opens in this design.

Dielectric thickness determines the probability of TDDB, and variations in that thickness can be spatially correlated across a wafer. That makes it highly likely that many interconnect failures would cluster in a particular region. It is unclear how Cerebras detects these shorts and avoids using the failed interconnects.

Ultimately, the argument is that you have a design that is expensive to begin with and also ages extremely quickly.

FOMC前瞻：短期科技股、半导体仍然承压

结论先说：我认为这次FOMC大概率不加息，但Warsh会继续放鹰。短期科技股、半导体，我依然维持偏空判断。

1. 水多了加面，面多了加水。

市场对10月加息的预期很低，维持利率不变，很难算额外利好。

但如果美联储表现得过于鸽派，市场提前交易宽松，美债收益率下降、股市上涨，金融条件反而放松，控制通胀就更难。

所以，暂停加息的同时维持强硬措辞，既能压住宽松预期，也给后续政策留出空间。

2. 后续加息路径，我重点看原油。

美联储最终要看CPI、PCE和就业数据，而原油是影响短期通胀路径的重要变量。

再往下推，油价受到中美俄博弈、中东局势和OPEC+供给政策的影响。美联储可以调整利率，却无法直接控制能源供应。

油价持续高位，紧缩压力就难以消退；油价明显回落，后续通胀压力才可能缓解。当然，能否结束加息，还要看核心通胀和就业是否配合。

3. 最终落到科技股、半导体的估值压力。

如果鹰派表态推动实际利率和融资成本走高，市场愿意给AI的估值倍数就可能下降。

高增长预期的芯片公司面临估值压缩，依赖外部融资的AI基础设施公司，还要面对庞大资本开支的融资压力。

业绩可以继续增长，股价也可能因为估值压缩而下跌。

所以我的交易思路依然是：短期保持谨慎，反弹更倾向于减仓，或等待做空条件确认。
